title: VolFill: Single-View Amodal 3D Scene Reconstruction with Volumetric Flow Matching
claim: Our generative approach recovers complete scenes including hidden surfaces from one image, while pixel-aligned baselines leave holes, layering artifacts, or noise.
layout: Large hero panel left; right 2x2 sample gallery above a 4-way baseline comparison row
description: The left half is a large 3D point-cloud rendering of an indoor dining room reconstructed from one unseen image. The input photo sits in the top-left corner, and a small mesh inset sits at the bottom-right. Surfaces visible in the input keep their photo colors, and hidden geometry recovered by the method is drawn in flat blue. The blue fills floors, walls, and areas behind furniture. A legend at the bottom left explains the brown and blue dots. The right half is a gray rounded panel. Its top has a 2x2 grid of further scenes, each with a small input thumbnail beside a blue-and-color reconstruction. Below the label 'Same scene, same view:' is a row of four cards: MoGe2, LaRI, NOVA3R, and VolFill (ours). The ours card has a blue outline, and the baselines show holes, layered artifacts, and noisy points.
caption: VolFill recovers the complete 3D scene, including surfaces hidden from the camera, from a single image. Geometry seen in the input view keeps the photo’s color; hidden geometry recovered by VolFill is shown in blue. Left: an unseen indoor image, as a point cloud and as a mesh extracted directly from the predicted TUDF grid. Top right: more qualitative samples. Bottom right: on the same scene and view, pixel-aligned MoGe2 leaves holes behind occluders, LaRI produces layered artifacts, and NOVA3R yields noisy, disintegrated points, whereas VolFill produces sharp and complete geometry.
abstract: Reconstructing the complete geometry of a scene from a single RGB image remains challenging, especially when inferring hidden structures where visual evidence is incomplete. We introduce VolFill, a generative framework that predicts the 3D structure of the complete scene rather than relying on traditional pixel-aligned regression. Our method utilizes a hybrid 3D VAE to compress sparse truncated unsigned distance function grids into a compact latent space, paired with a latent Diffusion Transformer that denoises this representation to recover the complete scene. We condition the generation on a geometry foundation model, leveraging rich spatial priors for robust reasoning. Unlike existing methods limited by per-ray constraints or unstructured point-cloud queries, VolFill provides a structured representation that supports direct surface extraction and occupancy queries at scale. Extensive experiments on the SCRREAM and NRGB-D datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms current amodal baselines, providing a robust foundation for holistic spatial understanding.
